title: A directed limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps is spectral, with spectral projections
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). Then $X$ is a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and every projection $p_i$ is spectral: $p_i^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2Z (label lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), stated there for a cofiltered index category; a directed set is the special case used here
